# VIORA Customer Data Processing Agreement — Template (Draft)

> **Draft only.** This template must be completed for the named customer, reconciled with the Master Services Agreement and reviewed by qualified Kenyan counsel (and EU counsel where GDPR applies) before signature. It is not an executed agreement.

## 1. Parties

This Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is entered into on [effective date] by:

- **Controller:** [Customer legal name, registration number, registered address, privacy contact]
- **Processor:** [VIORA contracting legal entity, registration number, registered address, privacy contact]

Each is a Party and together the Parties.

## 2. Scope and precedence

2.1 This DPA applies when Processor processes Personal Data on behalf of Controller to provide the Services described in Schedule 1.

2.2 The main services agreement remains in force. For personal-data processing matters, this DPA prevails to the extent of conflict.

2.3 The Parties shall comply with applicable data protection law, including the Kenya Data Protection Act, 2019 and regulations, and GDPR where applicable.

## 3. Definitions

“Personal Data”, “Data Subject”, “Processing”, “Controller”, “Processor”, “Personal Data Breach”, “Special Category Data” and “Supervisory Authority” have the meanings given in applicable Data Protection Law. “Subprocessor” means a third party engaged by Processor to process Personal Data on behalf of Controller.

## 4. Controller obligations

4.1 Controller determines and documents the purposes and lawful basis for processing and provides required notices to Data Subjects.

4.2 Controller warrants that its instructions, data collection, disclosures and use of the Services comply with applicable law.

4.3 Controller shall not instruct Processor to process Personal Data unlawfully and shall promptly notify Processor of changes to instructions.

4.4 Controller is responsible for the accuracy, lawfulness and minimization of Personal Data supplied to Processor.

## 5. Processor obligations

5.1 Processor shall process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Controller, including instructions concerning international transfers, unless required by applicable law. Where legally permitted, Processor shall inform Controller of such legal requirement before processing.

5.2 Processor shall ensure that persons authorized to process Personal Data are bound by confidentiality obligations.

5.3 Processor shall implement appropriate technical and organizational measures described in Schedule 2, taking account of the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing and the risks to Data Subjects.

5.4 Processor shall not sell Controller Personal Data or use it for independent advertising. Any product-improvement or AI use beyond Controller's documented instructions requires a separate documented purpose, lawful basis and agreement.

5.5 Processor shall make available information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance and shall support reasonable audits under clause 11.

## 6. Subprocessors

6.1 Controller authorizes only the subprocessors listed in Schedule 3 for the stated services and data categories.

6.2 Processor shall impose written data-protection obligations on each Subprocessor no less protective than this DPA and remains responsible for its Subprocessors' performance to the extent required by law.

6.3 Processor shall provide [30] days' notice before adding or replacing a Subprocessor, including its identity, service and processing location. Controller may object on reasonable data-protection grounds within [15] days. The Parties shall work in good faith to resolve the objection; if unresolved, Controller may discontinue the affected feature or terminate the affected Services without penalty, subject to the main agreement.

## 7. Data-subject rights and assistance

7.1 Processor shall promptly notify Controller if it receives a request from a Data Subject relating to Controller Personal Data, unless prohibited by law.

7.2 Processor shall not respond to the request except on Controller's documented instructions or as required by law.

7.3 Taking account of the nature of processing, Processor shall provide reasonable technical and organizational assistance to enable Controller to respond to requests for access, correction, objection, erasure, restriction and portability.

7.4 Processor shall assist Controller with security obligations, breach assessment, DPIAs and prior consultations to the extent required by applicable law and reasonably possible.

## 8. Security and confidentiality

8.1 Processor shall maintain the measures in Schedule 2 and review them periodically.

8.2 Processor shall restrict access to authorized personnel on least-privilege principles and remove access when no longer required.

8.3 Processor shall protect Personal Data in transit and at rest using appropriate encryption, maintain secure authentication and privileged-access controls, monitor security events, patch vulnerabilities and test recovery procedures.

8.4 Processor shall not represent a control as implemented unless it is deployed and supported by evidence. Any agreed remediation plan shall identify owner and target date.

## 9. Personal Data Breach

9.1 Processor shall notify Controller without undue delay and, in any event, within [24] hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Controller Personal Data, unless a shorter period is required by law.

9.2 The notice shall, to the extent then known, describe the nature of the breach, affected data and Data Subjects, likely consequences, containment/remediation, contact point and further information schedule.

9.3 Processor shall preserve relevant evidence, investigate, mitigate and provide reasonable updates. Processor shall not notify a regulator or Data Subject on Controller's behalf unless instructed or legally required.

9.4 Controller remains responsible for determining and making notifications to regulators and Data Subjects, with Processor assistance, unless the law allocates a duty directly to Processor.

## 10. International transfers

10.1 Processor shall not transfer Controller Personal Data outside the approved locations in Schedule 1 unless Controller has authorized the transfer in writing and the Parties have documented a valid transfer mechanism and required safeguards.

10.2 Processor shall provide information reasonably necessary for Controller's transfer assessment, including destination, recipient, purpose, data categories and safeguards.

## 11. Audit and compliance information

11.1 Processor shall provide reasonable information, policies, certifications and independent audit summaries relevant to this DPA upon request.

11.2 Controller may conduct an audit no more than once per year, or following a material incident or regulator request, on reasonable notice, subject to confidentiality, security and other customers' rights.

11.3 Audits shall be proportionate and avoid access to other tenants' data, secrets, source code or unrelated confidential information. Where direct inspection would create undue risk, independent assurance may be provided.

## 12. Return and deletion

12.1 On termination or expiry of the Services, Processor shall, at Controller's choice, return Controller Personal Data in a commonly used machine-readable format or securely delete it, within [30] days unless otherwise agreed.

12.2 Processor may retain data only to the extent required by law or subject to a documented legal hold. Retained data shall be isolated, access-restricted and deleted when the retention obligation ends.

12.3 Backup copies shall expire under the documented backup retention schedule. Processor shall prevent restored backups from reintroducing data previously deleted by applying deletion records before restored systems are made available.

12.4 Processor shall provide written confirmation of completion on request.

## 13. Term, liability and termination

13.1 This DPA begins on the effective date and continues while Processor processes Controller Personal Data.

13.2 The Parties shall allocate liability in the main agreement subject to mandatory provisions of applicable law.

13.3 A material breach of this DPA that is not remedied within [30] days after written notice may permit termination of the affected Services, without prejudice to other rights.

## 14. General

14.1 Changes to processing purposes, data categories, subprocessors or transfer locations shall be documented in writing.

14.2 This DPA does not reduce any Data Subject right or statutory obligation.

14.3 Notices under this DPA shall be sent to the contacts in Schedule 1.
